data.title: Gradient
data.tagline: Blend colors gradually across an area
data.description: A gradient moves smoothly between two or more colors. It can add depth, direction, or emphasis to a background and illustration. Keep text contrast stable across the whole blend, and use a flat color when the gradient adds no meaning.

use: Show a value range or heat scale
Add depth to a decorative surface
avoid: Place text over a region with changing low contrast
Use a gradient on every surface
Treat a decorative blend as a data scale

lessonPractice.title: A hero uses a blue-to-purple gradient. Its white heading reads well in the center but nearly disappears at the light end. How should it be fixed?

options.label: Adjust color stops or the text region for readability across the full area and provide a solid fallback
options.feedback: Every gradient position can sit behind the heading, so the entire text region must preserve contrast.

options.label: Add more saturated colors so the gradient looks stronger and overpowers the text issue
options.feedback: Stronger color variation further competes with copy and cannot replace contrast checks across the background.

options.label: Repeat the same gradient across cards, buttons, and footer to create site-wide consistency
options.feedback: Repeating a focal effect weakens hierarchy and spreads the same contrast risk to more content.

data.agentPrompt: Keep the blue-purple hero gradient but check every area behind the heading, adjusting stops, overlay, or placement for readability and adding a solid fallback. Do not spread it across the page; retest themes and mobile wrapping.
